answer_1.quote: we introduce a new task of controllable simile generation (CSG) -generating a simile with multiple simile elements ... and benchmark this task with the proposed CSG model Similor
answer_1.outputs: generated simile sentences containing tenor, vehicle, comparator, ground, and optional context

answer_2.quote: For automatic evaluation, we first use Perplexity (PPL) ... As for simile evaluation, we compute the proportion of sentences containing comparator words (%Comp.) ... we also use Simile Conf. to evaluate the figurative meaning of the generated results

answer_4.quote: Then, three crowdsource evaluators are asked to rate model results in four categories: 1) Fluency (Fluen.). Whether the sentence is fluent and grammatical; 2) Creativity. How well the sentence is figurately meaningful; 3) Consistency (Consi.). Whether the generated vehicle has shared properties with the pre-specified tenor; 4) Overall. How good is the simile overall?
answer_4.guideline: Evaluators score each generated simile on Fluency, Creativity, Consistency, and Overall on a 1‑4 scale.
